items.title: Algebraic braid relations do not imply unitarity
items.statement_or_definition: A Yang–Baxter operator or algebraic Hecke parameter need not define a unitary braid representation. On X=C with R=2I_(X⊗X), the Yang–Baxter equation holds and the induced B₃ generators all act by 2, but no positive-definite inner product makes 2I unitary. At the root Hecke normalization (T_i−v)(T_i+1)=0, the same scalar assignment is a representation at v=2.
proof_obligations: Check invertibility and YB, apply the actual braid-group theorem, verify the root Hecke normalization, and rule out every positive inner product.

items.title: Unitary fusion category
items.statement_or_definition: A unitary fusion category here is a finite semisimple rigid complex tensor category with simple unit, equipped with a conjugate-linear contravariant involution † on morphisms satisfying (g∘f)†=f†∘g†, (f†)†=f, and (λf)†= ar λ f†. Each finite-dimensional endomorphism *-algebra has a C*-norm ‖x†x‖=‖x‖²; tensor product preserves † and the associator and unit constraints are unitary. A braiding is extra structure; when present as a unitary braiding it satisfies c†=c⁻¹. Rigidity supplies evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the zig-zag identities; those maps are not asserted to be unitary isomorphisms.
proof_obligations: Specify the finite semisimple rigid complex base, dagger axioms, C*-positivity, tensor compatibility, and which structural maps are required to be unitary; do not label evaluation maps unitary.

items.title: Fusion multiplicity space
items.statement_or_definition: For simple charges a,b,c define N_ab^c=dim_C Hom(a⊗b,c) and V_ab^c=Hom(a⊗b,c). For f,g∈V_ab^c, define ⟨f,g⟩ by f∘g†=⟨f,g⟩ id_c; the next local theorem proves this is a finite-dimensional positive-definite Hermitian inner product. Multiplicities N_ab^c may exceed one.
proof_obligations: State the domain, codomain, multiplicities above one, and induced inner product convention.

items.title: Unitary ribbon data
items.statement_or_definition: A unitary ribbon structure is a ribbon structure in the sense of the root twist/ribbon definition, on a unitary braided fusion category, whose twist components are unitary. It includes the balancing identity and dual-compatibility condition; it is additional data beyond fusion rules or a braid-group representation.
proof_obligations: Restate the exact root ribbon/twist equations and verify the dagger compatibility used to call the twist unitary.

items.title: Modular nondegeneracy
items.statement_or_definition: In a unitary ribbon fusion category, an object x is transparent when c_(y,x)∘c_(x,y)=id_(x⊗y) for every simple y. The category is modular (has nondegenerate braiding) when its transparent objects are exactly finite direct sums of the tensor unit.
proof_obligations: Define double braiding on every simple summand and prove that the transparent objects are closed under direct sums. Do not infer modularity from a Yang–Baxter representation alone.

items.title: Topological spin
items.statement_or_definition: For a simple charge a, the topological spin θ_a is the unique scalar satisfying θ_a^ribbon=θ_a id_a, where θ^ribbon is the twist component. Uniqueness and existence follow from End(a)=C id_a.
proof_obligations: Show the twist endomorphism belongs to End(a) and has unit modulus under the unitary-ribbon hypothesis.

items.title: Fusion multiplicity spaces are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces
items.statement_or_definition: For every simple a,b,c in a unitary fusion category, V_ab^c=Hom(a⊗b,c) is finite-dimensional and the scalar determined by f∘g†=⟨f,g⟩id_c is a positive-definite Hermitian inner product, linear in f and conjugate-linear in g.
proof_obligations: Derive the scalar Hermitian pairing from dagger, show positive definiteness from the C*-identity, and use finite-dimensionality of the fusion category.

items.title: Ribbon evaluation and framed links
items.statement_or_definition: Assume AC_ω. In a unitary ribbon fusion category, for any simple color X and braids β∈B_n, β′∈B_m (n,m≥1), if their blackboard-framed X-colored closures are framed-isotopic, then their root ribbon evaluations t_n(β) and t_m(β′) are equal. Modularity is not required.
proof_obligations: Carry AC_ω exactly as required by the root framed-link theorem; modularity is not a hypothesis.

items.title: Multiplicity-aware fusion-tree basis
items.statement_or_definition: Choose an ordered binary fusion tree, an orthonormal basis in each vertex multiplicity space V_ab^c, a simple label on each internal edge, and one basis index at each vertex. Compose the vertex morphisms with the associators to obtain a fusion-tree vector in the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space. The preceding tree-basis theorem proves that these vectors form an orthonormal basis.
proof_obligations: Specify the parenthesization, all internal labels, each multiplicity index, and the composition convention.

items.title: Fusion-basis gauge change
items.statement_or_definition: A fusion-basis gauge change chooses a unitary matrix G_ab^c in each multiplicity space V_ab^c. With the convention that new basis columns equal old basis columns times G, the recoupling and exchange matrices transform as F′=G_R⁻¹FG_L and R′=(G_ba^c)⁻¹R G_ab^c.
proof_obligations: Check dimensions and unitarity of each change-of-basis matrix; distinguish basis gauge from changing the braided category.

items.title: R-symbol as a channel exchange map
items.statement_or_definition: For simple a,b,c let c_(a,b):a⊗b→b⊗a be the braiding. On V_ab^c=Hom(a⊗b,c), define the channel-exchange map R_ab^c(f)=f∘c_(a,b)⁻¹∈V_ba^c. The R-symbol is its matrix in the chosen orthonormal multiplicity bases. This pullback convention fixes the orientation of R-coordinates.
proof_obligations: Give the typed pullback formula and record the exchange-orientation convention.

items.title: Fusion-tree dimension recursion
items.statement_or_definition: Fix simple charges a₁,…,aₙ and simple total charge d, with the empty tensor equal to 1. For the recursively composed left-associated fusion-tree vectors, all admissible internal simple labels and multiplicity-basis indices give an orthonormal basis of Hom(a₁⊗⋯⊗aₙ,d); its dimension is the sum over admissible internal labelings of the product of vertex multiplicities. The recurrence is m₀(d)=1 if d=1 and 0 otherwise, m₁(d)=1 if a₁≅d and 0 otherwise, and mₙ(d)=Σ_e mₙ₋₁(e)N_{e aₙ}^d.
proof_obligations: Prove orthonormality/completeness of all multiplicity-aware tree vectors and the zero/one-input recurrence by semisimple decomposition.

items.title: F-symbol as a recoupling matrix
items.statement_or_definition: For simple a,b,c,d, set H_L=⊕_e V_ab^e⊗V_ec^d and H_R=⊕_f V_bc^f⊗V_af^d, with their left- and right-tree orthonormal bases. Let α_(a,b,c):((a⊗b)⊗c)→a⊗(b⊗c) be the associator. The F-symbol matrix F_d^{abc}:H_L→H_R is defined by the coordinate identity L_(e,μ,ν)∘α⁻¹=Σ_(f,ρ,σ) F_d^{abc}[(f,ρ,σ),(e,μ,ν)]R_(f,ρ,σ), where L and R are the corresponding composite tree morphisms. Every internal charge and multiplicity index is retained.
proof_obligations: Fix left/right tree ordering, associator direction, row/column convention, and all multiplicity indices.

items.title: Fibonacci fusion data and chiral convention
items.statement_or_definition: Fix labels 1,τ with 1⊗a=a⊗1=a and τ⊗τ=1⊕τ. Set φ=(1+√5)/2, F^{τττ}_1=[1], F^{τττ}_τ=[[φ⁻¹,φ⁻¹ᐟ²],[φ⁻¹ᐟ²,−φ⁻¹]], R^{ττ}_1=e^(−4πi/5), and R^{ττ}_τ=e^(3πi/5), with every unit-involving coordinate the identity. In this fixed chiral convention the F and R data are unitary and satisfy every pentagon and both hexagons; the proof below checks every nontrivial sector explicitly.
proof_obligations: Verify F/R unitarity, every four-τ pentagon sector, all unit-input cases, and both hexagon sectors with exact phase identities.

items.title: Gauge covariance of braid actions
items.statement_or_definition: For each fixed input list and total charge, applying a unitary gauge change at every internal fusion vertex conjugates every braid-word operator by the induced fusion-tree basis unitary. The pentagon and two hexagons ensure the tree-basis exchange operators satisfy the Artin relations; therefore the resulting unitary braid representations are unitarily equivalent. Expectation values are unchanged when states and measurement operators are transformed by the same unitary.
proof_obligations: Prove the adjacent Artin relations from naturality, both hexagons and the pentagon, then prove word conjugacy and expectation invariance.

items.title: A Hecke parameter does not certify a positive unitary structure
items.statement_or_definition: At v=2, the type-A Hecke algebra H_v(3) has a one-dimensional representation T₁↦2,T₂↦2. It satisfies the quadratic and braid relations but is not unitary for any positive-definite Hermitian form. Thus an algebraic Hecke specialization alone does not certify a positive unitary module or a unitary quotient; this example makes no claim about separately supplied *-structures or other parameters.
proof_obligations: Check the exact v-normalized Hecke relations at v=2 and show norm expansion for every positive form.

items.title: Worked Fibonacci and Ising braid matrices
items.statement_or_definition: For each displayed two-dimensional three-anyon sector in the fixed Fibonacci and Ising conventions, compute B₁=diag(R₁,R₂) and B₂=F B₁F. Both pairs are unitary and satisfy B₁B₂B₁=B₂B₁B₂. Their projective generator orders are 10 in the Fibonacci sector and 4 in the Ising sector.
proof_obligations: Display both matrix pairs, verify unitarity and both Artin identities, and compute projective orders exactly.
